data.cultural_impact: The name 'Athi' holds cultural significance in various aspects of Hindu society. In the Hindu epic Mahabharata, Bhagavad Gita, when Arjuna asked Lord Krishna about the origin and end of the universe, Lord Krishna mentioned the concept of Prana or breath which is present from creation till the end of the universe. In contemporanery Hindu literature, it is also believed that using the name of God (in this case, Lord Shiva) preserves one's life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name 'Athi' has deep spiritual significance as it represents the very essence of life and existence itself. Lord Shiva, who is known as the God of death and life, is also considered as the giver of breath or life. Hymns and mantras related to Lord Shiva often include the name 'Athi', acknowledging the divine source of all life. Furthermore, in Hindu philosophy, each breath we take is a reminder of the divine presence and the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth. Thus, the name 'Athi' offers a profound reminder of the interconnectedness of all life and the divine source of our existence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Athi, in Hinduism, represents the embodiment of wisdom and knowledge. The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Athiti', meaning 'the one who knows beyond'. It symbolizes the quest for eternal knowledge and enlightenment.
